question: Has the engine-cooling fault on Ocean Star happened before on this vessel or on others of the same class or technical manager?

rows.quote: 9 h lost to a seawater cooling pump failure on 2 Aug
rows.statement: Ocean Star lost 9 hours to a seawater cooling pump failure.

rows.quote: Delay due to engine cooling fault mid-voyage
rows.statement: Ocean Starlight had an engine cooling fault mid-voyage, which caused delay.

rows.quote: HT cooling water outlet temperature high alarm on ME at 0340 LT
rows.statement: The main engine HT cooling water outlet temperature high alarm activated at 0340 LT, and load was reduced.
About 6 hours were lost due to the engine cooling fault.
The seawater cooling pump seal was leaking.

rows.quote: Main engine stopped 0130-1330 LT due to seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failure.
rows.statement: The main engine of M/V OCEAN STAR stopped due to a seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failure.
rows.verification_basis: no independent source: INC-201 shares this fact's origin (vessel:V001)

rows.quote: Following repeated seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failures on Meridian 8500 class vessels this year (Ocean Star, Ocean Pearl),
rows.statement: Seawater cooling pump mechanical seals have repeatedly failed this year on Meridian 8500 class vessels, including Ocean Star and Ocean Pearl.

rows.quote: the cooling fault was in the auxiliary engine fresh water cooler,
rows.statement: The sender corrects the June cooling fault on MV Silver Tern to the auxiliary engine fresh water cooler, not the main engine seawater pump.
The delay attribution for the MV Silver Tern cooling fault remains 7 hours.
rows.verification_basis: no independent source: INC-094 shares this fact's origin (org:Harbourline Ship Management)

input.query: MATCH (i:Incident)-[:ON_VOYAGE]->(v:Voyage)-[:OPERATED_BY]->(x:Vessel) WHERE i.type CONTAINS 'cooling' RETURN i.evidence_id AS evidence_id, i.type AS type, i.status AS status, i.reported_utc AS reported_utc, i.attributed_delay_hours AS delay, v.evidence_id AS voyage, x.name AS vessel, x.vessel_class AS cls, x.technical_manager AS tm
input.reason: Search cooling incidents fleet-wide across vessels, class and manager; no typed tool searches by type across vessels.

thinking: I'm setting aside Ocean Starlight since it's a different vessel, a Nordwave Atlas 6000. Silver Tern shares the manager but not the class, and its fault was corrected to the auxiliary engine fresh water cooler, though that correction isn't verified and I'm treating it as superseding the earlier finding. Coral Crest is the same class but I'm dropping it. For "current" I'll go with INC-201 as the latest fault.

headline.text: Yes. Ocean Star had an earlier confirmed engine cooling fault (INC-118, 2 Aug 2026, 9 h) before the latest one (INC-201, 6 Oct 2026, 12 h). Ocean Pearl, same class and same manager, has a confirmed one (INC-077, May 2026, 10 h). Silver Tern, same manager but a different class, has a confirmed one (INC-094, June 2026, 7 h).

interpretation.text: I took 'the fault' to be Ocean Star's most recent Engine cooling fault, INC-201 on VG-1042, reported 6 Oct 2026. I searched all incidents of type 'Engine cooling fault' in the graph. Ocean Star is V001, class Meridian 8500, technical manager Harbourline Ship Management.

confirmed_facts.text: Same vessel: Ocean Star had a Confirmed Engine cooling fault on VG-0981, reported 2026-08-02 from the master's report, with 9 h attributed. The agent message says '9 h lost to a seawater cooling pump failure on 2 Aug'.

cited_values.value: 9 h lost to a seawater cooling pump failure on 2 Aug

confirmed_facts.text: Same vessel, latest event: INC-201 on VG-1042 is Confirmed, reported 2026-10-06, with 12 h attributed.
Same class and same manager: Ocean Pearl (Meridian 8500, Harbourline) had a Confirmed Engine cooling fault on VG-0866, reported 2026-05-09, with 10 h attributed.

Same manager, different class: Silver Tern (Kestrel 4000, Harbourline) had a Confirmed Engine cooling fault on VG-0844, reported 2026-06-03, with 7 h attributed. See the unverified correction below about the component.

unverified_reports.text: The Harbourline bulletin of 2026-10-09 says: 'Following repeated seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failures on Meridian 8500 class vessels this year (Ocean Star, Ocean Pearl),'. It is unverified, and it is the only source for that statement.

cited_values.value: Following repeated seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failures on Meridian 8500 class vessels this year (Ocean Star, Ocean Pearl),

unverified_reports.text: The master's noon report of 2026-10-06 for INC-201 is unverified because there is no independent source. It says: 'Main engine stopped 0130-1330 LT due to seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failure.' That gives the same component (a seawater cooling pump) as the August failure.

cited_values.value: Main engine stopped 0130-1330 LT due to seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failure.

unverified_reports.text: Ocean Pearl's master reported in a noon report of 2026-10-02 an HT cooling water high-temperature alarm, about 6 h lost, and a leaking pump seal. These are unverified and not linked to any incident. They would be a second Ocean Pearl event in October, after INC-077 in May.

Harbourline sent an unverified correction on 2026-10-21. It says the Silver Tern June fault was in 'the auxiliary engine fresh water cooler,' and not the main engine seawater pump, and that the 7 h attribution is unchanged. The correction supersedes INC-094 on the component, so Silver Tern's fault was probably a different failure mode from Ocean Star's.

cited_values.value: the cooling fault was in the auxiliary engine fresh water cooler,

inferences.text: Seawater cooling pump failures look like a recurring problem in the Meridian 8500 class under Harbourline. This rests on Ocean Star failing twice (Aug and Oct), Ocean Pearl failing in May, and the class bulletin. The component for the two Ocean Star events is stated only in unverified messages.
inferences.based_on: Three confirmed incidents on two Meridian 8500 vessels, plus the unverified manager bulletin naming a repeated seal failure.

exclusions.text: Coral Crest (Meridian 8500, Eastpoint Technical Services) INC-041 is Dismissed, so it did not happen. It is also a different manager.
Ocean Starlight INC-160 is excluded. It is a different vessel (Atlas 6000, Nordwave Marine) with a similar name, not Ocean Star and not in its class or manager group.

data_gaps.text: Only the incident and message records loaded in the graph were searched. Events before 2026 or never reported would not appear.

recommended_checks.text: Get the maintenance or technical report for Ocean Star's 2 Aug and 6 Oct failures, to confirm both involved the seawater cooling pump mechanical seal.
Ask Harbourline whether the 9 Oct bulletin sets out corrective actions for Meridian 8500 vessels. Also check whether Ocean Pearl's 2 Oct report was logged as an incident.

not_checked: Whether any bookings or later voyages of Ocean Star are affected by these faults.
